name: Republic of India

areaKm2.note: world_1960 India polygon = ~3,205,000 km2 computed on the sphere (mid). High = the official 3,287,263 km2 incl. all of claimed Jammu and Kashmir; low ~ area actually administered.

population.note: OWID (HYDE/UN) India 1971 = 558.1M (high); COW NMC v7 tpop 1971 = 551.2M; 1971 census (1 March) 548.2M (low). Mid ~555M for December 1971.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share India 1971 = 19.9% (1971 census definition gives ~19.9%).

activePersonnel.note: CIA Directorate of Intelligence memorandum "India-Pakistan: Comparative Capabilities in a New Military Confrontation", 13 Sep 1971, table "Military Personnel and Equipment as of Mid-1971" (p. 9): army 1,092,000, air force 78,200, navy 33,000 = 1,203,200 (high). Wikipedia war infobox gives Indian Armed Forces 825,000-860,000 (Palit 1998 p. 44; Cloughley 2016) (low). COW NMC v7 milper 1971 = 1,560,000 (https://correlatesofwar.org/wp-content/uploads/NMCv7.zip), which appears to include paramilitary, so not used. BSF and other paramilitary excluded.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: Territorial Army (~40,000) plus ex-servicemen with reserve liability. The CIA memo notes India lacks reserves of pilots and technicians. Border Security Force and state armed police (paramilitary) excluded.

supportPersonnel.note: Everything outside the infantry P roles: air force 78,200 and navy 33,000 (CIA mid-1971 table), plus armour, artillery (2,560 pieces), engineers, signals, logistics, staffs and training establishments of the 1.09M army. Mid = active minus P roles.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess: India never mobilised beyond ~1.2M against 555M people; WWII British India raised ~2.5M volunteers from ~390M (0.6%). Total-war ceiling set at 2-6% given a largely agrarian, low-income population.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Reconstruction from the CIA order of battle (mid-1971): 14 infantry divisions, 1 armoured division, 32 independent brigades and 47 battalion-size units. 14 x 9 battalions + ~120 battalions in independent brigades/units, x ~800 riflemen.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: 7.62 mm Ishapore SLR, Indian-made, era-typical; good recoilless and anti-tank weapons

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: long-service volunteer army, 1962 and 1965 combat veterans

count.note: 10 mountain divisions (CIA mid-1971) of ~9 battalions at ~800 riflemen plus the parachute brigade (Tangail drop, 11 Dec 1971). Light, mule-supported infantry.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: light mountain equipment, 75 mm pack howitzers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: specialist mountain and jungle troops, Eastern Command

count.note: CIA Directorate of Intelligence memorandum "India-Pakistan: Comparative Capabilities in a New Military Confrontation", 13 Sep 1971, table "Military Personnel and Equipment as of Mid-1971" (p. 9): artillery including self-propelled guns 2,560.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: 25-pdr, 5.5 inch, Soviet 130 mm M-46, 75 mm mountain guns

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional Regiment of Artillery

count.note: CIA Directorate of Intelligence memorandum "India-Pakistan: Comparative Capabilities in a New Military Confrontation", 13 Sep 1971, table "Military Personnel and Equipment as of Mid-1971" (p. 9): 1,075 medium tanks (T-54/T-55, Vijayanta, Centurion, Sherman) and 269 light tanks (PT-76, AMX-13) = 1,344.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: T-55 and Vijayanta a match for the Pattons (CIA memo: "greatest relative gain" since 1965); Shermans and AMX-13 obsolete

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: 1965 armour veterans; Basantar and Longewala

count.note: CIA Directorate of Intelligence memorandum "India-Pakistan: Comparative Capabilities in a New Military Confrontation", 13 Sep 1971, table "Military Personnel and Equipment as of Mid-1971" (p. 9): 600 armoured personnel carriers (OT-62 TOPAS, BTR series).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Soviet-bloc tracked and wheeled APCs, no IFVs

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mechanised infantry newly formed

count.note: CIA Directorate of Intelligence memorandum "India-Pakistan: Comparative Capabilities in a New Military Confrontation", 13 Sep 1971, table "Military Personnel and Equipment as of Mid-1971" (p. 9): MiG-21 170 + Gnat 167 = 337 (16 interceptor squadrons). Wikipedia air war article: IAF ~650 aircraft overall; 161 serviceable aircraft in the east vs 16 PAF.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: MiG-21FL supersonic, Gnat agile but subsonic day fighter

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: 1965 veterans; limited night and all-weather training

count.note: CIA Directorate of Intelligence memorandum "India-Pakistan: Comparative Capabilities in a New Military Confrontation", 13 Sep 1971, table "Military Personnel and Equipment as of Mid-1971" (p. 9): Su-7 139 + HF-24 55 + Hawker Hunter 98 + Canberra 54 = 346; Mysteres in the 163 "miscellaneous" (high).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Su-7 and Hunter era-typical, Canberra aging

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: ~4,000 sorties in the west and 1,978 in the east (air war article)

count.note: CIA Directorate of Intelligence memorandum "India-Pakistan: Comparative Capabilities in a New Military Confrontation", 13 Sep 1971, table "Military Personnel and Equipment as of Mid-1971" (p. 9): 161 helicopters (Mi-4, Alouette III); used for the Meghna heli-bridge.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: unarmed transport and utility types

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Meghna heli-bridge (Dec 1971) lifted a brigade

count.note: Naval war article infobox (Indian Navy): 1 light carrier (Vikrant), 2 light cruisers, 3 destroyers, 14 frigates, 5 ASW frigates (Petya). Low 20 if the Petyas count as corvettes. CIA mid-1971 table: 2 cruisers, 1 carrier.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: CIA: most ships old and of British origin; Vikrant a WWII hull

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: carrier operations and blockade of East Pakistan

count.note: CIA memo: 8 Osa missile boats, 2 Polnocny landing ships, 5 motor gunboats acquired from the USSR since 1965; naval war article lists 6 Osa boats and 2 landing ships in action; plus minesweepers and patrol craft. Reconstruction.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Osa boats with P-15 Styx anti-ship missiles sank PNS Khaibar (Operation Trident)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: first combat use of ship-launched missiles in the region

count.note: CIA Directorate of Intelligence memorandum "India-Pakistan: Comparative Capabilities in a New Military Confrontation", 13 Sep 1971, table "Military Personnel and Equipment as of Mid-1971" (p. 9): 4 F-class (Foxtrot/Kalvari) submarines; one under major repair (CIA memo).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: modern Soviet diesel-electric boats

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: submarine arm only formed 1967

count.note: Educated guess: batteries. CIA memo: air defence strengthened by Soviet SA-2 SAMs (number not given); perhaps 15-25 SA-2 sites around Delhi, Bombay, Calcutta and air bases plus army and air force AAA (L/60, L/70 Bofors, 3.7 inch) batteries.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: SA-2 era-typical, AAA dominant

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: most IAF losses in the east were to ground fire on the other side; Indian AAA claimed several PAF aircraft

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: Manekshaw delayed the war to the dry season and planned a 13-day lightning campaign to Dacca; good joint air-land-sea coordination in the east

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: long-service volunteer army with strong regimental identity

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: national cause after 10 million refugees; Soviet treaty backing

weapons.note: Anchor: between 8 (1943) and 9 (1985). Evidence: T-55, SA-2 SAMs, Styx missile boats, but much WWII-era kit (25-pdr, Shermans)

armor.note: Anchor: 8 (rolled homogeneous armour). Evidence: T-54/55, Vijayanta; no composite armour

ships.note: Anchor: 8 (carriers, radar, submarines). Evidence: Vikrant light carrier, Foxtrot submarines, Osa missile boats; no nuclear submarines

fortification.note: Anchor: 8. Evidence: concrete defences on the Punjab border (Ichhogil Canal on the Pakistani side), field fortification

logistics.note: Anchor: 8 (motor transport, rail). Evidence: rail-fed army, trucks, mule trains in mountain divisions, helicopter lift

communications.note: Anchor: 8 (radio at company level). Evidence: VHF radios at company level; no satellite links

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 8 = radar. Evidence: early-warning radars, Canberra PR photo-reconnaissance; no satellites

air.note: Anchor: air 8 = 1943, 9 = 1985. Evidence: MiG-21FL Mach 2, Su-7; no BVR missiles in use

cyber.note: No military computer networks; anchor cyber 9 = 1990 networks.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex 1971 = 1,924,810 thousand current US$; World Bank GDP 1971 = US$67.35bn (https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/IND/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD?date=1970:1972&format=json) -> 2.9% (low/peacetime). Wartime December 1971 higher; mid 3.2%.

industrialShare.note: World Bank NV.IND.TOTL.ZS India 1971 = 22.4% of GDP.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) India 1971 = 70.5%. Share 70.5% (range 67.0-74.0%) -> 0.295 (0.26-0.33).

annualCohort.note: Males reaching military age per year = male population 288,103,704 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN 1971) x share of males aged 15-19 10.535% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y 1971) / 5 = 6,070,520 (https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/IND/indicator/SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y?date=1971&format=json). Males only; range +/-10%.

artillery.note: Educated guess: Indian Ordnance Factories guns and howitzers per year (75/24 mountain gun, 25-pdr successors).

armor.note: Educated guess: Vijayanta tanks from the Heavy Vehicles Factory, Avadi (licensed Vickers Mk 1, production from 1965-66); wartime rate per year.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess: HAL licence production of MiG-21FL/M (Nasik, Koraput) and Gnat (Bangalore) per year.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess: HAL HF-24 Marut per year; CIA memo: 53 delivered since 1965.

helicopters.note: Educated guess: HAL Chetak (Alouette III licence) per year.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: Leander-class frigates at Mazagon Dock (first, Nilgiri, commissioned 1972): about one every two years.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: Surfaced roads in India c. 1971 (total road network ~1 million km, under half surfaced).

railKm.note: Educated guess: Indian Railways route length c. 1970-71 ~59,800 km (broad, metre and narrow gauge).

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Major ports: Bombay, Calcutta/Haldia, Madras, Visakhapatnam, Cochin, Kandla, Mormugao, Paradip, Tuticorin.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: India ~2.5M GRT of merchant shipping c. 1971 (Shipping Corporation of India plus private lines) x ~1.5 dwt/grt.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: Eastern campaign advanced ~250 km to Dacca in 13 days across riverine terrain, using helicopter lift and captured routes.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: India had ~70-80M working bullocks and buffaloes plus ponies, mules and camels in the early 1970s livestock censuses; the army used mules in mountain divisions.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS estimates via OWID: India 1971 = 0. First test (Smiling Buddha) 18 May 1974.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, local supply, fortified border cities and strong population support; depth large but no climate the Pakistani invader is unadapted to.

notes: Snapshot date 3 December 1971 (Pakistani pre-emptive air strikes; India-Pakistan war of 1971, 3-16 December). Population convention: everything inside the hb:1960:India polygon (Indian-administered Kashmir included; Sikkim a protectorate, excluded). Main source for the order of battle is the declassified CIA intelligence memorandum of 13 Sep 1971 (https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-0000399238), table as of mid-1971; the IISS Military Balance 1971-72 and Sisson and Rose, War and Secession (1990), could not be fetched and are not cited line by line. Theatre deployment for the battle agent (CIA memo): ~200,000 troops opposite West Pakistan, ~100,000 opposite East Pakistan, ~150,000 on the China border, ~600,000 elsewhere. The eastern offensive used nine infantry divisions (war article) plus ~175,000 Mukti Bahini (not counted here; they belong to the Bangladesh provisional government). Paramilitary (BSF, Assam Rifles) excluded from activePersonnel; COW milper 1,560,000 likely includes some of them. Infantry splits are reconstructions from division and battalion counts (grade C). Ratings and tech use the SOURCES.md rubric and anchors.
